subject: Future Tech
title: Lidar: Seeing with Lasers
description: A fast breakdown of Lidar: Seeing with Lasers for builders.

hook.text: Lidar fires millions of laser pulses per second and measures the reflections.

buildup.text: Each pulse bounces off objects and returns. The time delay reveals distance.

discovery.text: Lidar can detect objects 300 meters away with centimeter accuracy. It works in darkness and doesn't care about shadows.

twist.text: Early lidar cost $75,000 per unit. Now solid-state lidar costs under $500.

climax.text: Most AV companies use lidar as their primary sensor. It's the eyes of the self-driving car revolution.

punchline.text: A million laser beams per second, painting the road ahead.

quiz.question: How does lidar measure distance?
options: By measuring laser pulse return time
